text.p: Triangle Pharmaceuticals Inc said Monday it exercised its option to acquire a license from Mitsubishi Chemical Corp for the rights to MKC-442 worldwide except in certain East Asian countries, including Japan, China and Taiwan.
MKC-442, a drug candidate intended for the treatment of HIV infection and AIDS, is a molecule that binds to an enzyme called reverse transcriptase and blocks its normal functioning.

The company said additional data from an ongoing clinical trial for MKC-442 is being presented at a conference in Atlanta. In this trial, MKC-442 "was well-tolerated and only one patient, receiving the lowest dose...experienced a rash."

A Triangle spokesman said issues including drug metabolism, viral resistance and interactions with other HIV drugs will need to be explored before definitive efficacy studies of MKC-442 in combination therapy can begin. The company said they intend begin studies later this year.
A company spokesman said the clinical phase of the first of pharmacokinetic interaction studies is completed with the Merck & Co Inc protease inhibitor, Crixivan.

Triangle said the license agreement will require payment of a license initiation fee and certain milestone and royalty payments to Mitsubishi. Final details of the licensing agreement are still being negotiated, it added.
